comment: Generator families. By default (generators.root = "package") script and preset.dir come from this package; generators.root = "project" switches python families to projectScript/projectPreset (the research tree geometry/). The built-in engine "primitive"/"js" needs no Python.

families.title: FCC cell (sphere + necks)
families.description: Parametric FCC cell of a porous medium: spheres at the nodes + necks; the raw STL from CAD/CSG is cleaned and checked automatically.
families.notes: The clean STL is written by stl_qa --clean-out. For meshing use {cleanOut}: the raw STL may contain degenerate faces.

families.title: Channel with sphere packing (fluid + solid + named patches)
families.description: Two-region geometry: a channel filled with spheres, separate STLs for fluid/solid and named boundaries (inlet, outlet, walls, interface).
families.notes: fluid_patches.stl goes into snappyHexMesh as a surface whose patch names are already set (inlet/outlet/walls/interface); for cfMesh the names are carried over through renameBoundary in meshDict (see experiment exp-017).

families.title: Double-layer burner (solid + fluid)
families.description: Two regions: a solid frame and a flow passage; the output is 4 files — raw and clean STL for each region.
families.notes: Do not mesh the raw *_raw.stl files: use *_solid.stl and *_fluid.stl.

families.title: Sphere packing (table → STL)
families.description: Two-step generator: first a table of balls/contacts, then STLs of the solid frame and the flow passage with necks.
families.notes: The number of balls is set in params (or --max-spheres in the table CLI); for large packings STL generation may take minutes.

families.title: CAD geometry (CadQuery): block/channel/plate with spheres
families.description: CAD generator for complex composite shapes; a raw OCC STL is almost never watertight — cleanup is mandatory.
families.notes: Tessellation is controlled by angularTolerance in params (0.1 — accurate volume, 0.2–0.3 — for meshing); after generation clean up: stl_check({ stl, cleanup: true }).

families.title: Portable primitives (box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pipe, parts[])
families.description: Closed bodies written in plain JS — box, sphere, cylinder, cone (with an apex), pipe (hollow cylinder), and a parts[] assembly with per-part translate/rotate_deg/scale. No python, no project data.
families.notes: Generation and QA run on JS. Every body takes center_mm; each body or parts[] entry accepts translate_mm, rotate_deg (X then Y then Z, degrees) and a uniform scale. volume_mm3_theory is analytic.

families.title: Stratified channel (two liquids, horizontal interface)
families.description: A rectangular channel cut by the plane z = interface_z: lower.stl (bottom) and upper.stl (top), 12 triangles each, units mm. A built-in JS generator: no Python, no CAD, no project data.
families.notes: The plane is horizontal with no tilt; there is no porous filling — this is a clean stratified layer. Outputs: {outDir}/{name}.lower.stl and {outDir}/{name}.upper.stl (role fluid for both). For a two-phase/CHT problem the interface is better stitched by a conformal mesher (gmsh route D).

families.title: Blob foam (metaballs → isosurface)
families.description: Porous foam from overlapping “blobs”: a metaball field on a grid, an isolevel (or a bisection search for a target porosity), trimming by an analytic domain via SDF, marching cubes. It reproduces the Blender approach “metaballs + voxel remesh + Boolean Intersect” without Blender and without CAD; the report gives porosity, solid/pore-space connectivity and thickness distributions.
families.notes: Mesh {cleanOut}. Porosity is set by target_porosity (bisection on the isolevel) or by a fixed threshold. voxel_mm is the field resolution: step ≤ 0.1·r_min, otherwise the necks are lost. The domain is a cylinder along z or a box.

families.title: Lattice of spheres/cylinders (box-array)
families.description: A regular nx×ny×nz lattice of spheres or cylinders in a box: solid.stl (N closed shells) and container.stl (the box itself). A built-in JS generator, units mm — suitable for testing meshing outside the project.
families.notes: Parameters: container_mm, lattice [nx,ny,nz], shape (sphere|cylinder), radius_mm, height_mm (cylinder), margin_mm, segments/rings/sections. If the lattice spacing is smaller than the body size, a warning is written to the JSON: snappy will read the intersecting shells as one body.
